summary: Private research university in Tuzla, Istanbul, with 12 four-year bachelor's programmes taught 100% in English and a declare-your-major-later model.
about: Sabancı lists engineering, science, social science, management and visual arts programmes. Students can declare a major later through its Freedom to Declare Major model.

ib.text: IB Diploma: minimum 28 out of 45 (2025-26 list). Scholarships need more. Course Results alone are not listed as an entry route; contact Sabancı before relying on them.

languageOfInstruction.note: Programme list shows every bachelor's programme as 100% English. Applicants without English proof take a Foundation Development Year.

admissionRoutes.text: Sabancı lists a minimum Diploma score of 28 out of 45 for 2025-26. Meeting it is eligibility only; the page does not publish subject rules or a cut-off.
No IB Course Results route is listed. Applications without one of the accepted exams or diplomas at a valid score are not evaluated; ask Sabancı before applying.

notes: Documents: one accepted exam/diploma result, transcript signed by the school, motivation letter, recommendation letter, optional certificates and language proof. Pay a USD 30 application fee. SAT is not mandatory. Offers need a USD 2,000 non-refundable prepayment.
Fall 2026 timeline: applications opened 1 Jan 2026, early deadline 14 Mar 2026, final deadline 28 Aug 2026 at 16:00 Turkish time. Fall 2027 dates are not published.

English proof to skip the one-year Foundation Development Year: TOEFL iBT 85, PTE Academic 71, CAE/CPE grade C, or Sabancı's own ELAE stage 2 (70). Home and online tests are not accepted. No IB English exemption is stated, so ask.

Tuition for new international students in 2026-27: USD 36,500 a year before scholarships (25%, 40%, 50%, 60% or 75% tuition waivers). The page also shows USD 24,500 for non-scholarship students without explanation, so confirm. 2027-28 fees are not published.
You also need a Turkish high-school equivalency certificate (denklik) to register. Meeting the admission rules does not guarantee equivalency.
